source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — German, Grade 7
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). First published 2022, Revised 2024. Backfilled retroactively — skills already shipped in web/src/skills/germanG7/ before this record was written. Foreign language design (target A1/YCT2 proficiency). Structured as 9 real-world THEMES (Greetings/introduction, Family, My Surroundings/market, Time/important dates, Fun and enjoyment/weekends & holidays, Food and drinks/shopping, My Body/physical appearances, Weather and Environment/four seasons, Getting Around/neighborhood), each contributing one sub-strand to each of 3 strands: 1.0 Listening and Speaking, 2.0 Reading, 3.0 Writing (27+18+9 = 54 lessons plus 6 lessons for showcasing). This JSON models each strand as top-level with its 9 theme-linked sub-strands, mirroring the source's per-theme table layout rather than grouping by theme, since strand is the design's own primary organizing header.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Active Listening, Oral Expression (Theme 1: Greetings and Introduction — Basic Greetings)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify listening markers in a text for communication
listen actively for comprehension
use acquired vocabulary to communicate in varied contexts
appreciate the role of vocabulary in foreign language learning
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we show that we are listening?
How do we acquire vocabulary in a foreign language?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on greetings with peers (Assoziogram)
watch an audio visual on typical German greetings and match to given pictures
listen to a text on typical German greetings and simulate them with peers while observing social etiquette rules
role-play greeting and introducing oneself with peers using phrases like 'wie geht's? Woher kommst du? Mir geht es prima, danke gut..usw'
research on greetings from German speaking countries from various sources (online/offline) and make presentations to peers

subStrands.name: 1.2 Listening for Information, Interactive Speaking (Theme 2: Family — Nuclear Family)
specificLearningOutcomes: listen to texts for information
interact with peers on varied topics
value the role of listening texts in language acquisition
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we ensure we get all the needed information from a listening text?
How do we make our conversations interactive?
learningExperiences: watch audio visual of someone introducing their family (nuclear)
listen to texts and answer given questions on members of the family
introduce members of their nuclear family to classmates by their name, age and profession in plenary
research with peers how introductions are done in German-speaking countries and present in plenary
linkedLearningAreas: Religious Education and Social Studies: the family.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Active Listening, Oral Expression (Theme 3: My Surroundings — The Market Places)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify vocabulary related to the given context for learning
listen actively to varied speakers for communication
value the role vocabulary plays in language acquisition
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we show someone we are listening to them?
How do we acquire vocabulary in a new language?
learningExperiences: watch audio visual materials on the market place and mark the items being bought
listen to audios on the market place and answer given questions
role play situations in the market with peers
research on markets in Germany and present findings in a plenary
discuss with peers the need of following a budget while shopping at the market

subStrands.name: 1.4 Listening for Information, Interactive Speaking (Theme 4: Time — Important Dates)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify required information from listening texts
speak interactively on given topics
appreciate the role listening texts play in language acquisition
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we avoid distractions while listening to a text?
Which aspects can enhance understanding of a listening text?
learningExperiences: listen to given texts and answer given questions
practice with peers counting in German
discuss important dates in their lives (Geburtsjahr, Feste usw) with peers
research important dates in Kenyan and German history in groups and present in a plenary

subStrands.name: 1.5 Active Listening, Oral Expressions (Theme 5: Fun and Enjoyment — Weekends, Holidays)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify appropriate vocabulary in given texts
listen to texts for comprehension
value the role active listening plays in communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we acquire new vocabulary?
learningExperiences: watch an audio visual on leisure time activities and match to given pictures
listen to texts on holiday destinations and activities and answer given questions
talk about what they do on weekends and during holidays using expressions such as gern, lieber and am liebsten
research on a holiday destination they would like to visit and make a presentation on the same in a plenary
discuss in plenary appropriate weekend and holiday activities and which activities to avoid
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili: hobbies and leisure time activities.

subStrands.name: 1.6 Listening for Information, Interactive Speaking (Theme 6: Food and Drinks — Shopping for Food)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify required information from listening texts
speak interactively on given topics
value the role vocabulary plays in social interactions
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we make our conversations interactive?
learningExperiences: listen to texts and underline key words related to quantities (Kilo, Liter, Dutzend)
listen to texts and answer given questions on shopping
role play with peers different shopping situations (at the butchery, at the grocery store, at the supermarket etc)
make presentations in plenary on different shopping situations using acquired vocabulary

subStrands.name: 1.7 Active Listening, Oral Expressions (Theme 7: My Body — Physical Appearances)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify required vocabulary in given listening texts for comprehension
listen actively to varied speakers for comprehension
appreciate the role of adjectives in communication
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we describe someone's appearance?
learningExperiences: watch videos of people being described and match to given pictures
watch videos of people being described and underline the adjectives used
describe people using given pictures/flashcards/illustrations
make presentations describing their favourite people by their appearances using adjectives such as nett, freundlich, gross usw
discuss in plenary the appropriate ways of describing one's physical appearances

subStrands.name: 1.8 Listening for Information, Interactive Speaking (Theme 8: Weather and Environment — The Four Seasons)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify required information from listening texts
speak interactively on given topics
value the role of listening texts in learning
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we ensure we get all the needed information from a listening text?
learningExperiences: listen to an audio on weather and seasons and answer given questions
watch an audio visual on the different seasons in Germany and match to given flashcards
research and discuss with peers on which clothes go with which seasons
record themselves talking about the different seasons and changing weather patterns in Kenya and Germany and share in plenary for feedback
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: weather and climate change.

subStrands.name: 1.9 Active Listening, Oral Expressions (Theme 9: Getting Around — In the Neighborhood)
specificLearningOutcomes: identify necessary vocabulary for learning
listen actively to texts for learning
appreciate the role of vocabulary in a language
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you ensure keenness when listening to texts?
learningExperiences: watch a video on someone giving directions in German and note down prepositions of location
listen to an audio on giving directions and answer given questions
simulate giving directions around their neighborhood with peers using expressions such as 'wie komme ich..? Wo finde ich..?'
use city/area maps to give directions with peers
linkedLearningAreas: English and Kiswahili: prepositions of location.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Reading Aloud — Articulation (Theme 1: Greetings and Introduction — Basic Greetings)

keyInquiryQuestions: Why is reading aloud important?

read out members of their nuclear family to classmates by their name, age and profession in plenary

specificLearningOutcomes: identify essential information from a reading text

appreciate the role of reading comprehension in languages
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we get the intended message from reading texts?
learningExperiences: read given texts and answer given questions on dates and holidays
practice with peers counting in German by reading numbers aloud
discuss important dates in their lives (Geburtstag, Geburtsjahr, Feste usw) with peers

write simple dialogues on giving directions with peers
simulate giving directions around their neighborhood with peers using expressions such as 'wie komme ich..? Wo finde ich..? Danke'
